collection_method: Read-only GitHub repository, issue-search, issue, comment, event and pull-request GET requests through the GitHub connector. Embedded code and reproductions were treated as evidence and not executed. No packages, agents, models, tools, MCP servers, workflows or target systems were run or contacted.

selected_records.title: [BUG] Responses chaining ignores agent session ids when Langfuse is disabled
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: controlled cross-agent session isolation failure when tracing was disabled
selected_records.provider_attribution: CAMEL OpenAI Responses-compatible backend state; no provider-side fault or live provider execution established.
selected_records.assessment: A local reproduction reports two configured agent sessions sharing one backend and agent B reusing agent A's previous response identifier. The issue closed without a linked commit in its public event record. This is cross-session state use, not authenticated autonomous coordination or a task-result exchange.

selected_records.title: [BUG] ChatAgent.reset() never clears OpenAIModel previous_response_id chain state, so a pooled agent's next task can continue the wrong conversation
selected_records.provider_attribution: CAMEL AgentPool and OpenAI Responses-compatible backend state; the local reproduction made no network calls.
selected_records.assessment: A provider-free reproduction shows a reused pooled worker inheriting the prior task's response-chain identifier and omitting its own system prompt. An open unmerged pull request contains regression tests. This is one reused configured worker crossing task boundaries, not distinct autonomous participants.

selected_records.title: [BUG] DeepSeekModel's per-agent reasoning cache is never cleared by ChatAgent.reset(), leaking reasoning_content into unrelated later tasks
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: controlled cross-task reasoning-cache leak on a reused agent
selected_records.provider_attribution: CAMEL DeepSeek adapter cache behavior; the reproduction used local response objects and no provider call.
selected_records.assessment: A local test reattaches task A reasoning to an unrelated task B message when a pooled agent emits the same short text. A public commenter says they reproduced the leak and traced the lifecycle. This is strong cross-task content transfer/use evidence, but still one reused framework object rather than independently verified agents.

selected_records.title: [BUG] CAMEL creates MCP servers with no authentication, exposing agent history and tool-driven command execution to unauthenticated clients (CWE-306, CVSS 9.8)
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: reported unauthenticated agent-history access, state mutation and model-mediated tool execution on an operator-exposed server
selected_records.provider_attribution: CAMEL-generated MCP server and registered host tool; DeepSeek was used only as the server-side model in the reported command-execution path.
selected_records.assessment: The report says its read-only and state-change assertions were dynamically reproduced and that an unauthenticated client could drive a registered host tool through the agent. The issue remained open and no merged patch was identified when observed. This is a material server authorization defect, not inter-agent coordination or a new swarm.

selected_records.title: Lack of Data-Control Separation in Environment Memory Bus Leads to Indirect Prompt Injection and System-wide Lateral Contamination
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: unverified static claim of low-trust input propagating across role memory
selected_records.provider_attribution: MetaGPT Environment/Role architecture; no model or provider execution evidence.
selected_records.assessment: The issue describes a plausible cross-role indirect-prompt-injection path but explicitly provides no runtime logs. It closed automatically after inactivity. Without an original run, downstream output or side effect, it is a static threat-model control rather than an observed exchange.

selected_records.title: [Bug] Asynchronous State Pollution due to Unisolated Global Config Singleton
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: unverified static claim of shared configuration pollution across concurrent roles
selected_records.provider_attribution: MetaGPT configuration architecture; no model or provider execution evidence.
selected_records.assessment: The report alleges concurrent roles share mutable configuration but supplies no runtime trace or reproduction output. It closed automatically after inactivity. General supporting comments do not independently verify this repository-specific path.

novelty_result: No previously unreported rogue swarm confirmed. CAMEL records preserve cross-session identifier, system-prompt and reasoning-content reuse across configured task boundaries, while the MetaGPT records are static-only claims. The unauthenticated CAMEL MCP server report is material but concerns external access to one configured agent or workforce rather than autonomous participant coordination.
limitations: Searches were capped at 30 newest-updated rows and overlap; this is not a complete issue census.
Issue bodies, comments and pull requests are public tracker evidence, not authenticated agent telemetry.
Configured pooled workers, framework roles and MCP clients are not independently verified autonomous participants.
The MetaGPT security claims lack runtime logs and closed after inactivity; they must not be presented as confirmed exploits.
Open issues and unmerged pull requests do not prove vulnerable public deployments or continuing agent activity.
No code, package, reproduction, agent, model, tool, MCP server, workflow or target service was executed or contacted.

Advancement requires an unpublished original real-run exchange with independently corroborated autonomous participants, transferred task work actually used by a distinguishable recipient, and evidence that the coordination itself crossed operator authorization rather than reflecting pooled object state, backend caches, server exposure or a static threat model.
redactions: No executable reproduction bodies, example secrets, commands, target endpoints, personal addresses, private logs or tool payloads are included.
Assessments retain public record links, timestamps and body hashes while summarizing mechanisms at a domain level.
